summary: 8-point inverse synthesis filter bank (MDCT-style) for audio decoding. Loop 1 iterates 8 times reading input samples a3[0..56] at stride 8, applies window/rotation math and writes 8 floats into a stack buffer; if all 8 inputs are zero it short-circuits and copies the DC product a3[0]*v6[0] to all 8 outputs. Loop 2 iterates 8 times, combines the 8 transformed samples, and writes 8 interleaved bytes into the output buffer a5 using a byte lookup indexed from a4 and base a1+0x11C+128, converting float to int via CRTFtol. Returns the last byte written. The ABI lead names it Audio_Mixing_8_point_Inverse_MDCT.

local_names.a1: audio context; offset 0x11C read to compute output lookup base
local_names.a2: object holding window-coefficient float buffer at +0x50
local_names.a3: 8 input samples at stride 8 (a3[0], a3[8], ..., a3[56])
local_names.a4: index buffer selecting the output byte offsets within a5

operations.description: v36 = *(DWORD*)(a1 + 0x11C) + 128: compute the base index used for the final output byte lookup.
First loop, 8 iterations (counter v34 = 8): step v6 over the window-coefficient buffer (a2+0x50), step a3 over the 8 input samples, and write 8 float results into the v7 stack buffer.
Zero-sample short circuit: if the OR of all 8 input samples a3[0..56] is zero, skip the transform and copy the DC product a3[0]*v6[0] to all 8 output slots.

Full synthesis path: combine the 8 windowed samples using the inline rotation constants 1.4142135, 1.847759, 2.613126 and 1.0823922 into the 8 output slots; the packet's fact table flags four read-only float globals (flt_5ACEA4, flt_5B0818, flt_5B081C, flt_5B0820) as read by this function.
Second loop, 8 iterations: combine the 8 transformed samples (v25 buffer) and for each output byte index write the looked-up byte value into a5 at a5 + *(DWORD*)(a4 + 4*index).
CRTFtol converts the float rotation constant 1.4142135 to int; the (value + 4) >> 3 & 0x3FF expression forms a constant byte-lookup offset added to v36 for each output byte.
Return the last byte written into the output buffer.
